figures.alt: Hotel Wi-Fi reaches one travel router, which makes its own Wi-Fi for four devices

figures.caption: **Figure 1. Two jobs, one box.** It joins the hotel Wi-Fi, just like a phone would. Then it makes a Wi-Fi network that belongs to you.
figures.alt: Job one: the travel router joins the hotel Wi-Fi. Job two: it makes your own Wi-Fi for your devices.

figures.caption: **Figure 2. Your Wi-Fi is a few steps away.** The hotel's Wi-Fi often comes from down the hall. Your own Wi-Fi comes from the desk, right next to you.
figures.alt: The hotel access point is down the hall, behind a wall. The travel router sits on the desk, a few steps from your devices.

figures.caption: **Figure 3. One radio for each job.** The top radio joins the hotel. The bottom radio runs your own Wi-Fi. In the middle, the box sends everything out as if it were one device.
figures.alt: Inside the box: one radio talks to the hotel, one radio talks to your devices, and in between everything leaves as one device

figures.caption: **Figure 4. Sign in once, not on every device.** Only the travel router meets each new hotel. Your devices see the same network every trip, so they join on their own.
figures.alt: Without a travel router, every device signs in at every hotel. With one, only the router signs in and your devices join by themselves.

figures.caption: **Figure 5. Help for gadgets with no browser.** A TV stick or a game console can struggle with a sign-in page. On your own Wi-Fi, it never sees one.
figures.alt: A TV or game console alone cannot open a hotel sign-in page. Behind a travel router, it joins your Wi-Fi with no sign-in.

figures.caption: **Figure 6. The hotel counts one.** Usually, every device behind the travel router shares that one spot. The limit shown is an example. If a hotel still blocks it, ask the front desk.
figures.alt: With a limit of two devices, three of five are locked out. With a travel router, the hotel counts one and all five get online.

figures.caption: **Figure 7. One on the list, many in the room.** The hotel sees one device. Everything you carry sits behind it.
figures.alt: The hotel's list shows one device in your room. Behind it sit five of your devices.

figures.caption: **Figure 8. Your devices stay on your side.** On hotel Wi-Fi, your devices may share a network with strangers. Many hotels keep guests apart, but you can't tell which. Behind the travel router, your devices sit on your own network.
figures.alt: On hotel Wi-Fi alone, your devices sit among strangers' devices. Behind a travel router, they sit on your own network and strangers stay outside.

figures.caption: **Figure 9. Three steps, done once.** Give your network a name and a password, then join each device to it. After that, they join by themselves.
figures.alt: Three steps at home: plug it in, give it your own name and password, then join each device once.

figures.caption: **Figure 10. Three things to pack.** The travel router, its power cord, and a short network cable in case the room has a wall jack.
figures.alt: Pack three things: the travel router, its power cord, and a short network cable.

figures.caption: **Figure 11. Pick the hotel network.** On your phone, open the travel router's settings. Choose the hotel's network from the list, and the router joins it.
figures.alt: From your phone, open the travel router's settings and pick the hotel network. The travel router joins it.

figures.caption: **Figure 12. One sign-in covers everyone.** Open a web page on a phone joined to your travel router. The hotel's page shows up. Accept it once, and every device is online.
figures.alt: Open a web page on a device joined to your travel router. The hotel sign-in page appears. Accept it once and every device is online.

figures.caption: **Figure 13. A cable is steadier.** The cable carries the hotel side. The travel router's Wi-Fi then works only for you and your devices.
figures.alt: Over Wi-Fi, the travel router reaches a far, shared hotel signal. With a cable to the wall jack, the hotel side is steady and the router's Wi-Fi is all yours.

figures.caption: **Figure 14. Use the internet port.** The cable from the wall goes into the port meant for the internet. The jack may show the same sign-in page as the Wi-Fi.
figures.alt: Run the cable from the wall jack to the travel router's internet port. The router's Wi-Fi then serves your devices.

figures.caption: **Figure 15. Slow in, slow out.** The travel router shares what the hotel gives. It can make things steadier, but not faster.
figures.alt: A slow hotel line stays slow. The travel router passes on the same speed; it cannot make the line wider.

figures.caption: **Figure 16. Check for two radios.** A one-radio model takes turns talking to the hotel and to you, so it runs slower.
figures.alt: A one-radio model uses the same radio for the hotel and for you, taking turns. A two-radio model gives each job its own radio.

figures.caption: **Figure 17. Known beats nearby.** Your devices usually pick the network they know. To put one on the hotel Wi-Fi, turn the travel router off, or tell that device to forget your network.
figures.alt: With the travel router on, your phone stays on the network it knows. Turn the router off and the phone joins the hotel Wi-Fi.

figures.caption: **Figure 18. The wall works both ways.** Other guests can't reach your devices. Your devices also may not find things on the hotel network, like a room TV you cast video to, because they are on a different network.
figures.alt: The travel router is a wall that works both ways: other guests cannot reach your phone, and your phone cannot reach the hotel's room TV.

figures.caption: **Figure 19. One tunnel for every device.** Set up on the router, the VPN covers everything behind it.
figures.alt: With a VPN on the travel router, everything your devices send crosses the hotel network scrambled, on its way to the VPN service.

figures.caption: **Figure 20. Two easy wins.** Set it up before you leave, and keep it where your devices can hear it.
figures.alt: Set it up at home, not late at night in a hotel. Put it out in the open, not in a bag or a drawer.
